entries.summary: Added the shared rule that a required choice may select only an actually available option; Penance and Property Dues inherit that rule from current game authority.
Current v0.7.1 card authority explicitly states that Neutral Observers overrides other Gambit-order effects but does not change Tactic order, so Fog may still determine Tactic order.
Current v0.7.1 authority resolves the Redemption and Attrition destination conflict through the Golden Rule that the more specific conflicting effect controls.

PR #1435 fixed the reviewed Gambit/Tactic destination follow-up sequence by preserving terse referents, promoting explicit destination authority, and requiring concrete destination values; #1441 generalized recency-aware conversational retrieval.
PR #1435 fixed the exact reviewed destination follow-up chain, including terse corrections such as 'no, their destinations'; #1441 generalized the conversation-focus behavior.
The opening Gambit/Tactic distinction turn belongs to the exact reviewed destination conversation fixed and regression-covered by PR #1435.
This reviewed follow-up is part of the same exact Gambit/Tactic destination conversation fixed and regression-covered by PR #1435.

Added a deterministic current-v0.7.1 scope precheck for the reviewed strategy, lore/history, costume/visual-design, morality/design, and version-history request families. These requests now return source-free out_of_scope results before corpus retrieval or model-budget reservation, while deck-construction and Leader rules questions continue to the canonical Rules Arbiter.

These reviewed interactions had correct substantive rulings, current authority, sufficient retrieval, and only an overly weak classification. PR #1419 tightened the current v0.7.1 explicit-versus-inferred boundary and added deterministic classification-contract coverage; later behavior revisions retain that boundary.

Force the complete v0.7.1 Surveillance/Interference procedure into Intelligence interaction retrieval and require the Arbiter to preserve prerequisites, separate costs and timings, destinations, replacement/pass choices, revision rights, and no-reopen rules. The exact reviewed Surveillance -> already-face-up commitment -> Interference-cost follow-up chain is regression-covered against Direct Interference and Interference-after-Surveillance authority.
Promote the governing v0.7.1 Normal Capture and Front Line authority for Territory-capture questions and require those passages to appear in the top three retrieval results.

Promote the current v0.7.1 Shock and Awe card and Conflicting victory benefits rule for same-victory restriction questions, including terse follow-ups; include War Crimes authority when the overlap is named.

Promote the current v0.7.1 Treaty Articles and Peace Treaty timing authority for sixth-ratification questions and terse timing follow-ups, with Accepted or Refused Terms authority when that path is named.

Promote the current v0.7.1 Mystics progression and Transmutation procedure for second-Rite ability questions, natural procedure paraphrases, and terse follow-ups; preserve Spirit Walker authority when that Leader is part of the active topic.
Expand tied opening-roll and first-player phrasing to the current v0.7.1 Setup authority so the explicit 'Reroll ties' rule is retrieved rather than forcing an unnecessary provisional ruling.

Expand opening-Hand and setup query phrasing so the current v0.7.1 draw-four, discard-one, keep-three setup procedure appears in the top retrieval results for starting-draw and starting-Hand-size questions without contaminating normal turn draws or Intelligence Mission startup.

Recognize natural questions about when a played card is discarded and promote the current v0.7.1 Action-card destination rule: resolve the Action effect, then put the card in the Discard Pile unless it becomes an Asset or Overlay or its effect gives another destination, without overriding Gambit or Tactic destination authority.

The current v0.7.1 retrieval and prompt path now supplies the Quick Battle Reference, complete Battle Sequence, advantage/disadvantage authority, and Defensive Edge authority for the reviewed post-commitment game-state question. Regression coverage requires whole-sequence reconstruction and preserves the distinction between ordinary advantage on battle dice and Defensive Edge on tied battle totals.

Promote the v0.7.1 Golden Rules authority whenever a player asks which instruction controls a genuine specific-versus-general conflict, while retaining the normal battle sequence alongside it for battle-order questions.

Current v0.7.1 retrieval directly supplies Onward's During Movement permission together with the shared rule that movement which begins a battle ends that movement sequence and loses unused movement. The reviewed continuation and post-battle questions are now regression-covered without a new runtime behavior change.

Add a general ordered-reference rule for multi-object card text so pronouns such as 'that card' and 'it' remain bound to the most recent compatible object introduced by the instruction after already-resolved card movement. Good Faith therefore cannot silently switch those later references back to the source Asset after that Asset has been discarded.

The production session chronology shows 'What benefit does this give me?' immediately followed the Good Faith exchange despite a stale audit rationale describing a different prior topic. Current contextual retrieval preserves that real Good Faith referent and returns Good Faith as the first authority source; regression coverage now locks the exact continuity behavior.

Map the legacy phrase 'defender advantage' and close variants to the current v0.7.1 Defensive Edge authority. This prevents generic dice Advantage from outranking the controlling tie-break rule while leaving ordinary Advantage and double-Advantage questions unchanged.

Production session chronology confirms that 'Does it depend who owns the territory' immediately followed 'Explain fog of war'. Current v0.7.1 contextual retrieval keeps Fog of War as the first authority source, and the card explicitly keys its delayed Gambit/Tactic order to the Territory's controller. The exact reviewed continuation is regression-covered without a new runtime behavior change.

Current v0.7.1 retrieval supplies Command and Repel as the first two authority sources and also includes the complete Military rule that directly states Command may be gained during either player's turn and that newly gained Command may pay for an Aftermath Order. The existing explicit-classification prompt contract therefore covers the reviewed Commandant/Repel question; regression coverage locks that behavior without a new runtime change.

Current v0.7.1 retrieval returns the complete Purification rule first for the reviewed failed-Reserve question. That rule directly states that Purification checks the opponent's normal start-of-turn draw and that a failed Reserve draw or effect-generated draw does not trigger it. The existing explicit-classification prompt contract therefore covers the reviewed question; regression coverage locks the distinction without a new runtime change.

Production session chronology confirms that 'can you explain that more clearly' immediately followed the Deed-cost formula, while the historical answer incorrectly jumped backward to the earlier Front Line/Deed-ownership topic. Current v0.7.1 contextual retrieval and prompt prioritization preserve the immediate Deed-cost referent and retrieve the complete Deed-cost rule first, so regression coverage closes the reviewed failure without a new runtime change.

Promote current v0.7.1 Tiebreak Roll authority when battle-tie questions describe the procedure as a reroll rather than naming it. The current rule treats the Tiebreak Roll as a separate sudden-death roll: advantage, disadvantage, card effects, numerical modifiers, and previous battle totals do not apply unless a rule expressly modifies a Tiebreak Roll. Setup first-player tie rerolls remain on setup authority.

Current v0.7.1 retrieval returns the complete Rite of Crossing authority first for the reviewed completion question. The written rules directly state the next-turn completion condition, interruption/reset behavior, no same-turn completion rule, and paid-cost handling, so the answer is explicit rather than provisional.

Promote the detailed current v0.7.1 Ranger/Fieldcraft authority when Fieldcraft questions concern Territory control, Occupation, Capture, Defensive Edge, Last Stand bonuses, or Territory-derived limits. This supplies the explicit limitation that Fieldcraft does not alter those game states instead of leaving the Arbiter to infer from abbreviated ability text.

Current v0.7.1 retrieval directly supplies Safe Conduct and Political Capital for the reviewed interaction. Safe Conduct replaces the qualifying battle loss with withdrawal, while Political Capital is expressly conditioned on losing following refused Terms; the ruling is therefore explicit rather than provisional. No runtime change is required.

The reviewed broad Shock and Awe explanation had sufficient authority but omitted material conditions. Current v0.7.1 retrieval returns the complete Shock and Awe card first and the conflicting-victory rule alongside it, while the current whole-procedure prompt requires the Arbiter to preserve the complete sequence and its prerequisites, branches, restrictions, and destinations. The exact reviewed question is regression-covered; no new runtime change is required.

The reviewed no-contiguity ruling was correct and correctly classified as inferred, but its selected authority was too weak. Current v0.7.1 retrieval supplies the Front Line definition, Deed ownership-independence rule, and the specific purchase table together; those rules compel the no-contiguity result, while the current classification boundary correctly treats absence of a contiguity restriction as inference rather than explicit authority. No runtime change is required.

The reviewed remote-purchase ruling was correct and explicit, but the final selected source was weaker than the specific purchase authority. Current v0.7.1 retrieval returns Buying and buying out Deeds first; its purchase table expressly prices the case where the buyer neither controls nor occupies the Territory, with the Deeds rule also confirming ownership independence from position and control. No runtime change is required.

Future expansion and development-roadmap requests now use the deterministic current-v0.7.1 out-of-scope precheck before corpus retrieval or model-budget reservation. The exact reviewed Communism-expansion question is regression-covered, while gameplay uses of expand remain in scope.

Short counterfactual follow-ups such as the reviewed “What if I win instead?” now inherit the immediately preceding exchange before retrieval. This keeps the question on Margin Loan’s Gambit/Tactic battle branch, whose current v0.7.1 text directly returns collateral after a win, instead of drifting to unrelated generic victory authority or conflating the separate Action/banked loan branch.

The exact reviewed opponent-control wording now retrieves Fog of War as primary v0.7.1 authority. Current card text keys the ordering to the contested Territory’s controller and explicitly makes that player set their Gambit and choose their Tactics after the opponent. This closes the historical reversed-order answer without importing the retired v0.6.0 notion that control of the Overlay itself determines the order.

Historical or design-inspiration questions phrased as who a game element was designed after, based on, modeled after, inspired by, or what historical or real-world figure inspired it now use the deterministic current-v0.7.1 out-of-scope precheck before corpus retrieval or model-budget reservation. Gameplay questions about the same Leader, such as what the General does, remain in scope.

Questions that explicitly ask whether multiple controlled effects resolve one after another or at the same timing now retrieve the v0.7.1 Shared timing rule alongside the specific effect authorities. For the reviewed Fate’s Toll + Valor case, both cards remain primary sources while Shared timing directly supplies the missing ordering premise that each player chooses the order of effects they control; each effect still must satisfy its own printed condition when it resolves.

Current v0.7.1 retrieval returns Strategic Withdrawal first for the reviewed Aftermath question. The card directly states that after the normal retreat the losing player may take the additional movement and return one other controlled battle card to Hand, while the clearing rule says to follow a card-specific destination instead of the normal battle-card destination. The existing explicit-classification prompt contract therefore covers the reviewed ruling; regression coverage closes the historical provisional overclassification without a runtime behavior change.

Battle-card replacement questions now deterministically promote the v0.7.1 Replacing a Gambit or Tactic authority. When a named battle card is already the strongest source it remains first, and destination-focused replacement questions also promote battle-card clearing. Operational Reassessment therefore supplies its own Graveyard destination, the shared replacement rule preserves the Gambit role and passed-timing constraint, and normal Gambit clearing supplies the replacement card’s destination.

The reviewed follow-up asks whether a replacement can apply a Gambit effect whose reveal timing has already passed. Deterministic retrieval now promotes the replacement rule first; that rule explicitly says replacement does not reopen an earlier timing window and only still-available, unapplied effects may apply. Existing explicit-classification discipline therefore closes the historical inferred label.

A terse follow-up such as ‘Can I use this ability right now?’ now stops before model use when the immediate exchange does not identify one matching ability/effect/feature referent. The Arbiter asks for the missing ability and relevant timing state instead of speculating about unrelated factions or mechanics. A single clearly bridged named referent still flows through normal contextual retrieval.
